title: TAPPaaS Module Field Definitions
description: Defines the structure and valid values for module configuration JSON files (e.g., myModule.json)

description.description: Descriptive text that appears on the Proxmox summary page for the VM
description.example: Nextcloud file sharing and collaboration platform

version.description: Version of the module (not the TAPPaaS system). Used for tracking running versions and determining if upgrades exist.
version.note: Major < 1 indicates module is not production-ready

appVersion.description: Upstream application version deployed by this module. Optional but recommended. Distinct from 'version' (module semver). Treated as an informational string — no format enforced.
appVersion.note: Use the upstream project's own version string: semver, date-based, or tag (e.g. '33.0.3', '1.85.0', 'nightly')

releaseDate.description: Date when this version of the module was released
releaseDate.note: Automatically set to today's date by copy-update-json.sh if not present in source JSON

installTime.description: Timestamp when the module was installed, automatically set by copy-update-json.sh
installTime.note: Automatically set during install. Format: YYYYMMDD-HH:MM:SS (local time)

updateTime.description: Timestamp when the module was last updated, automatically set by `module-manager module modify`
updateTime.note: Automatically set on each update. Format: YYYYMMDD-HH:MM:SS (local time)

variant.description: RETIRED — superseded by 'environment'. Never write this field. Retained here only so a pre-migration config that still carries it is classified rather than reported as unknown; installs strip it (copy-update-json.sh del(.variant)).
variant.note: Was set when --variant <name> was used at install time, and until its retirement was also MIRRORED from --environment for suffixed environments. Everything that read it (provider pairing, name-suffix stripping) now reads 'environment'. A migrated site should carry no .variant at all: strip it with scripts/migrate-drop-variant.sh.

environment.description: Target environment this module was installed into (ADR-007 P5). Persisted by copy-update-json.sh when --environment <name> is used so `module-manager module modify`/`delete` can resolve the source module file and the environment. Not present for legacy/no-environment installs.
environment.note: Set automatically when --environment <name> is used at install time. Auto-managed by the 3-way merge — never adopted from the release source. The successor to 'variant', which is RETIRED. Also carries the name suffix for a non-default environment (<module>-<environment>.json) and selects the same-environment provider in resolve_provider_module.

maintainer.note: Typically a GitHub username prefixed with @

values.Development: Module is under active development, not ready for production
values.Testing: Module is being tested, may have issues
values.Production: Module is stable and ready for production use
values.archived: Module's VM was removed via `module-manager module delete --archive` but its config and PBS backups are kept for restore. Set automatically on archive; inspect-cluster.sh shows it as [archived] rather than NOT RUNNING.
values.external: VM/guest that exists on the cluster but is managed OUTSIDE TAPPaaS (e.g. pfsense, hassosova). A minimal config ({vmid, vmname, status:external, description}) registers it as known-but-unmanaged: no install/update/test/delete lifecycle applies, backup:vm ignores it unless explicitly added, and inspect-cluster.sh shows it as [external] rather than NOT IN CONFIG. Mirrors zones.json state=Manual.

rebootOk.description: May an UNATTENDED converge disrupt this module's guest — reboot it, or migrate it offline — in order to apply a declared change (ADR-020 D8)? A field's change class says a change NEEDS disruption; this says whether we are ALLOWED to cause it without a human present. It is therefore a property of the WORKLOAD, not of the field: a stateless front-end can be bounced at 03:00, a database only in a window. Default false, so silence never authorizes downtime.
rebootOk.note: Disruption is authorized iff '--allow-disruption' was passed (an operator, now: 'module-manager module update <m> --allow-disruption', or 'site-manager update --allow-disruption' for a run), OR rebootOk is true AND the scheduled run has automaticReboot (ADR-020 v0.10 D8). '--force' is a different lever: it proceeds past a refusal and never reboots. When a disruptive change is not authorized the converge applies everything else, prints a machine-parseable 'DEFERRED:' line and still exits 0; update-tappaas collects those into an end-of-sweep summary.

tier.description: Lifecycle role of the module (ADR-007b). Answers 'Can it be uninstalled?'. Orthogonal to 'source' — never collapsed into one enum (MECE). 'foundation' modules are critical platform components: they may only be installed into the 'mgmt' environment, are single-instance, and require --force to delete. 'app' modules are tenant-facing and deploy into any environment.

values.foundation: Critical platform module (mgmt-only, single-instance, --force to delete). Lint rule: source MUST be 'official' (or explicit --allow-fork override).
values.app: Tenant/environment-facing module — deployable into any environment, multi-instance across environments.

tier.note: Mandatory in authored module JSON (ADR-007b CR-04). The schema gives it a 'app' default so legacy module configs that predate ADR-007 still validate (back-compat); authored modules SHOULD set it explicitly.

kind.description: What type of workload the module is (ADR-022f D1) — equivalently, which Controller builds it. AUTHORED in the module's source JSON and adopted by deployments through the 3-way merge. Not what it runs on: that is its Host, named in `node` (ADR-022c D3).

values.vm: A virtual machine (KVM/QEMU) on a cluster member.
values.lxc: A Linux container on a cluster member.
values.machine: Its own system with an OS, not a Proxmox guest (ADR-026) — e.g. the satellite.
values.application: Software installed onto a Host, owning no system of its own; names its Host in `node` — e.g. backup.
values.device: Only network reachability is configured — no SSH, no checks.
values.module: LEGACY, never authored: ADR-007's object-type marker, once stamped into every deployed config. Migration 0004 removes it; it survives only where it is a config's sole module signal, so discovery can still find that module.

kind.note: Absent on modules ADR-022 does not classify yet — `cluster` and `templates` (the grouping concept is its own ADR); discovery finds them by their shape. Before #611 this field was the object-type marker, stamped "module" by install-module.sh; that stamping is gone.

source.description: Origin & trust of the catalog entry (ADR-007b). Answers 'Where does the catalog entry come from?'. Orthogonal to 'tier'. Normally INFERRED at deploy time from the repository the module is catalogued in (sourceMetadata lives in Site → repositories, CR-05); only set explicitly when the module file itself must pin it.

values.local: ⚪ Local — local dev, not in any catalog.

source.note: Optional. Defaults to 'official'. Lint rule (validate-module-tier-source.sh): tier:foundation requires source:official unless --allow-fork is given.

location.description: Absolute path to the module directory containing install.sh, update.sh, etc.
location.note: Automatically set by copy-update-json.sh based on the directory where the module JSON resides

dependsOn.description: List of services this module depends on. Each entry is a 'module:service' pair identifying which module delivers the service.
dependsOn.note: The installer validates that each referenced module is installed and provides the named service

integratesWith.description: List of OPTIONAL services this module integrates with if present. Same 'module:service' shape as dependsOn and wired by the same install/update/delete-service.sh scripts — but a provider that is not installed is silently ignored rather than blocking. When a provider is later added, its install auto-wires the pre-existing integrators.
integratesWith.note: Soft counterpart to dependsOn: missing provider = skip (no error); installed provider = same install-service.sh logic. Do NOT list a coordinate in both dependsOn and integratesWith. The two differ in LIFECYCLE, not reachability (#632): a cross-zone coordinate here earns the same network:rules auto-pinhole a dependsOn entry would.

provides.description: List of services this module provides. Service names only (the module is implicit from the JSON filename).
provides.note: Each listed service must have a corresponding services/<service>/install-service.sh and update-service.sh

config.description: Optional Pattern-A nesting (Pattern C hybrid). Groups per-service configuration under the '<module>:<service>' dependency coordinate instead of (or alongside) flat top-level fields. Purely a readability/authoring convenience: TAPPaaS NORMALIZES it to the flat form at deploy (copy-update-json.sh) and at validation (check_json), so all tooling still reads flat top-level fields. A module may be written fully flat (current form), fully Pattern-A, or mixed.

^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9-]*:[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-.description: Configuration for one declared dependency. The fields inside are ordinary module fields (cores, proxyDomain, …) scoped to that service.

rules: Every key in 'config' must also appear in 'dependsOn' (a config block for an undeclared dependency is an error).
A field must not appear in both the header and a config block, nor in two config blocks (ambiguous after flattening — rejected).
Multi-service header fields (e.g. zone0, vmname, vmid) stay at the top level — they are owned by the module, not a single service.
config.note: Convert between forms with module-format.sh (to-flat | to-config). Backward compatible: flat modules are untouched.

os.description: The operating system a system runs — ADR-022f's OS facet, held as its `id` (the freedesktop os-release ID); the family follows from it: debian, ubuntu, nixos → linux; windows → windows. For a VM it also drives cloud-init bootstrapping (the Debian vendor-data snippet). For a machine, `module adopt` reads it from /etc/os-release, and it selects the machine module (ADR-026 D7).
os.default: <auto-detected from image filename: debian-*, ubuntu-*, *nixos* -> matching value; else unknown>

values.debian: Debian-family cloud image (apt). Receives the tappaas-debian vendor-data snippet.
values.ubuntu: Ubuntu-family cloud image (apt). Receives the tappaas-debian vendor-data snippet.
values.nixos: NixOS template VM. No vendor-data snippet.
values.windows: Windows Server clone VM. Create-TAPPaaS-VM.sh builds and attaches a per-VM OOBE answer ISO. No cloud-init.
values.unknown: OS family is unknown. No vendor-data snippet.

os.note: Optional. If omitted, Create-TAPPaaS-VM.sh falls back to sniffing the 'image' filename. Set explicitly to override the sniff.

zone0.description: The security zone the FIRST network interface connects to; it must exist in zones.json. For a VM or LXC: which Proxmox bridge VLAN its virtual NIC is attached to. For a machine (kind: machine, ADR-026): which network its first physical NIC is cabled to — recorded, not yet enforced (connecting a machine's port on the switch is its own issue).
zone0.note: Zone determines VLAN tag. 'mgmt' is untagged traffic. camelCase only — no underscores or hyphens. ADR-007 P5: when zone0 is unset it DEFAULTS to the target environment's network.zone (read from config/environments/<env>.json); pre-cutover (no site.json/environments) it falls back to resolve_default_zone()'s behaviour. An explicit zone0 in the module JSON always wins.

zone1.description: The security zone the SECOND network interface connects to, if there is one; it must exist in zones.json. For a VM: which Proxmox bridge VLAN its second virtual NIC is attached to. For a machine: which network its second physical NIC is cabled to — recorded, not yet enforced.
zone1.note: Only used if bridge1 is defined. Hyphens are NOT allowed — use underscores.

address.description: How the mothership reaches a machine (kind: machine, ADR-026 D8.1): an IP address or FQDN, logged into as root with the mothership's key. Written by `module adopt`. A VM or LXC is reached by its name and zone instead and has no `address`.
address.note: Changing it records where the machine is now; it moves nothing.

management.description: Whether TAPPaaS runs a lifecycle against this module (ADR-022g): `managed` — it installs, updates, tests and deletes it; `unmanaged` — registered so the Site knows it exists, with no lifecycle. Absent means managed.

values.unmanaged: registered only; no install, update, test or delete

management.note: Recorded now; the sweep does not read it yet — it still takes a module out with `status: archived | external`.

module_structure.description: Standard files in a TAPPaaS module directory

install.sh.description: Installation script called with module name as argument

update.sh.description: Update script called periodically to keep module updated

<module>.meta.json.description: Optional, cluster:lxc only. Carries LXC-specific provisioning details that are intentionally NOT validated against this schema (so device/passthrough config stays flexible). Read by cluster:lxc Create-TAPPaaS-LXC.sh. A module declares cluster:lxc (not cluster:vm) in dependsOn; declaring both is rejected by install-module.sh.
<module>.meta.json.required: if cluster:lxc and the container needs passthrough/bind-mounts/non-default lxc options

gpu.description: Optional. GPU device passthrough. When present, the provisioner emits lxc.cgroup2.devices.allow entries and bind-mounts /dev/kfd and the render node into the container.

render_node.description: DRI render node name, e.g. renderD128

bindMounts.description: Optional. Host directories bind-mounted into the container as mpN entries. NOTE: containers with bind mounts cannot use pct snapshot — rollback is unavailable for these modules.

lxcOptions.description: Optional. Overrides for pct create defaults.

unprivileged.description: 0 = privileged (required for GPU passthrough), 1 = unprivileged. Default 1.

services/<service-name>/install-service..description: Script called when a module consuming this service is installed. Called with the consuming module name as argument.

services/<service-name>/update-service.s.description: Script called when a module consuming this service is updated. Called with the consuming module name as argument.

services/<service-name>/pinhole.json.description: Declares the network ports a service exposes. When a consumer module depends on this service across zones, network:rules synthesises an auto-pinhole rule per declared port (subject to the destination zone's pinhole-allowed-from policy). Issue #173.

ports.description: Network ports this service exposes for consumers in other zones.

port.description: TCP/UDP port number, or port range as a string (e.g. '8000:8010').

naming_conventions.module_name: Typically the main software product or capability being delivered
naming_conventions.vm_name: Same as module name by default
naming_conventions.hostname: Same as module name by default
